headline: A fast-moving cold front brings a burst of moderate to heavy rain, possible thunderstorms and gusty winds to northern San Diego County around 1 PM Thursday, with a risk of street flooding, before dry, cool weather returns Friday through Sunday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday night stays dry and cool with weak onshore breezes, scattered clouds around 3,000–5,000 feet and high clouds streaming in ahead of Thursday's storm. Mid-level clouds thicken over the coast and valleys toward early Thursday morning. Winds pick up over the mountain ridges late tonight, and a Wind Advisory is in effect until 4 PM Thursday for the San Diego, Riverside and San Bernardino County Mountains, the San Gorgonio Pass near Banning, and the Apple and Lucerne Valleys.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: On Thursday, a well-defined cold front sweeps in from the north: light rain is possible in northern Orange County and the Inland Empire as early as 7 AM, the main band of moderate to heavy rain hits there around 10 AM, reaches far northwestern San Diego County (including the Carlsbad area) around 1 PM, and arrives in San Diego itself between about 1 and 3 PM. Warm ocean water may add embedded thunderstorms, with downpours of 0.50 to 0.65 inch per hour possible, especially in the northwest part of the region, which could cause urban flooding, small stream rises and small rockfalls in the mountains; the band weakens as it moves south and inland, clearing Orange County and the Inland Empire around 3–4 PM and San Diego County by about 6 PM, followed by lighter, on-and-off showers with very little thunder risk. Gusts reach 15–30 mph at the coast and valleys as the front passes and 45–60 mph over the mountain ridges, passes and desert foothills, with winds turning westerly Thursday evening and easing by early Friday. Snow levels start above 7,500 feet (locally near 7,000 feet in heavier bursts), falling to about 7,000 feet late Thursday afternoon and 6,000 feet late Thursday night, with a few inches at ski-resort level and on high mountain passes but only about 0.1 inch to an inch of wet, heavy snow in Big Bear.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A few showers may linger in southwestern San Diego County through Friday morning before skies clear, and another weak disturbance keeps temperatures cooler than average Friday. A brief, weak warm-up on Saturday nudges afternoon highs up only a few degrees. Another weak system late Sunday into Monday has about a 40% chance of bringing much lighter rain, though some computer models keep it mostly dry. After a brief dry spell late Monday into Tuesday, another storm may arrive late Tuesday into Wednesday; models have trended slightly wetter, but they differ widely on its strength and timing, which will make a big difference in temperatures and rain.

coast: A northwest swell builds Thursday, raising surf to 4–6 feet with sets to 8 feet on west-facing beaches through early Friday, with strong rip currents and minor coastal flooding during high tide. King Tides peak next week, with tides above 7 feet possible as early as Saturday, Nov. 21. For boaters, a Small Craft Advisory runs from 4 AM Thursday to 10 AM Friday for waters out to 60 miles from San Mateo Point to the Mexican border, including San Clemente Island, with steep 5–8 ft seas and 20–30 knot gusts; winds start south-southwest Thursday and turn westerly by late afternoon, conditions improve later Friday, and seas are much calmer by the weekend.
watch_for: Heavy downpours of 0.50–0.65 inch per hour and possible thunderstorms as the front reaches northern San Diego County around 1 PM Thursday, with a risk of urban flooding.
Strong mountain, pass and desert-foothill gusts of 45–60 mph through Thursday afternoon (Wind Advisory until 4 PM).
Whether light rain arrives Sunday night into Monday (about 40% chance) and how the late Tuesday–Wednesday storm shapes up.
confidence: Forecasters lay out Thursday's storm timing in detail and expect dry, cool weather Friday through Sunday; confidence is moderate for light rain Sunday night into Monday and low on the details of the late Tuesday–Wednesday system.
